families.name: HTTP Status Codes
families.description: Standard response status codes used by HTTP clients, servers, gateways, and APIs.
entries: The server received the request headers and the client may continue sending the request body.
The server is changing protocols as requested by the client.
The request succeeded and the response contains the requested representation or result.
The request succeeded and created a new resource.
The request was accepted for processing, but processing has not necessarily completed.
The request succeeded and there is no response body to return.
The server fulfilled a valid range request with part of the selected representation.
The target resource has a new permanent URI.
The target resource is temporarily available at another URI.
The client should retrieve another resource with a GET or HEAD request.
A conditional request found that the cached representation is still current.
The resource is temporarily elsewhere and the client must preserve the request method.
The resource permanently moved and the client must preserve the request method.
The server cannot process the request because its syntax or framing is invalid.
The request lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.
The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.
The server did not find a current representation for the requested resource.
The request method is known but not supported by the target resource.
The server did not receive a complete request within the time it was prepared to wait.
The request conflicts with the current state of the target resource.
The target resource is intentionally unavailable and is likely to remain so.
The server refuses the request because a required Content-Length was not provided.
One or more request preconditions evaluated to false.
The request content is larger than the server is willing or able to process.
The request target is longer than the server is willing to interpret.
The server does not support the request content format.
The requested byte range cannot be satisfied for the selected representation.
This code is reserved by HTTP and cannot be assigned a future semantic meaning.
The server understood the content type and syntax but could not process the instructions.
The source or destination resource of a WebDAV method is locked.
A WebDAV method could not run because a dependent action failed.
The server is unwilling to risk processing a request that might be replayed.
The server refuses the request under the current protocol but may accept it after an upgrade.
The origin server requires the request to be conditional.
The client sent too many requests in a given period.
The server refuses the request because its header fields are too large.
Access to the resource is denied as a consequence of a legal demand.
The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.
The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.
A gateway or proxy received an invalid response from an upstream server.
The server is temporarily unable to handle the request.
A gateway or proxy did not receive a timely response from an upstream server.
The server does not support the major HTTP version used in the request.

families.name: MySQL Errors
families.description: Curated MySQL server and client errors with practical database troubleshooting.
entries: The server rejected authentication for the supplied user, host, or credentials.
The requested database name does not exist on the connected MySQL server.
A statement refers to a column that is not available in the resolved table or scope.
An insert or update would violate a unique index or primary-key constraint.
MySQL could not parse the SQL statement according to the active server grammar.
A statement refers to a table that is absent from the selected database.
A transaction waited longer than the configured limit to acquire a lock.
InnoDB detected a transaction deadlock and rolled one participant back.
The client could not establish the requested local or network connection to MySQL.

families.name: PostgreSQL Errors
families.description: Selected PostgreSQL SQLSTATE conditions and reliable diagnosis guidance.
entries: A statement violated a unique constraint.
A statement would leave a foreign-key reference without a matching row.
A null value was supplied for a column that does not allow nulls.
Text input could not be converted to the target PostgreSQL data type.
The referenced relation could not be resolved in the current database and search path.
The referenced column does not exist in the resolved relation or query scope.
PostgreSQL could not parse the SQL statement.
A transaction could not be serialized safely and was rolled back.
PostgreSQL found a cycle of transactions waiting on one another and aborted one.

families.name: SMPP Errors
families.description: Standard SMPP 3.4 command_status results for SMS platform integrations.
entries: The PDU contains an invalid message length.
The command_length field is invalid for the PDU.
The receiver does not recognize the command_id.
The command is not allowed in the current SMPP session state.
The session is already bound and cannot accept another bind.
The SMSC encountered an internal system error while handling the command.
The source address supplied in the PDU is invalid.
The destination address supplied in the PDU is invalid.
The supplied message identifier is invalid or unknown.
The SMSC rejected the bind request.
The password supplied during bind is invalid.
The system_id supplied during bind is invalid.
The message queue has reached its capacity.

families.name: PHP Errors
families.description: Stable PHP engine error and exception classes with focused debugging guidance.
entries: A value, return value, argument, or property does not satisfy a declared PHP type.
An argument has the correct type but an invalid value for the operation.
PHP could not parse source code because its syntax is invalid.
A function or method received the wrong number of arguments.
An integer division or modulo operation attempted to use zero as the divisor.
No arm of a match expression handled the supplied value.
An assertion evaluated to false and PHP was configured to throw.
A PHP warning or notice was converted into an exception by an error handler.

families.name: Laravel Errors
families.description: Normalized, stable Laravel failure concepts rather than application-specific stack traces.
entries: Laravel could not generate a URL because the requested named route is not registered.
The service container could not resolve a requested class or binding.
Eloquent rejected attributes that are not allowed for mass assignment.
Laravel rejected a state-changing web request whose CSRF token was missing or invalid.
The application has no valid APP_KEY for Laravel encryption services.
Laravel could not locate the named Blade view in its configured view paths.
The PHP process cannot write a required Laravel storage or cache path.
PHP autoloading could not find a class referenced by the Laravel application.
